clue.text: Hard worker having to accept a far from reasonable rise

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the word upward, so the letters for unreasonable run backwards

parts.note: someone far from reasonable is mad
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A hard-working labourer must put up with an unreasonable pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns MAD into DAM in this down clue; 'having to accept' only links A and DAM to the worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Adamant is an old name for an unbreakable stone, and figuratively means unyielding.

clue.text: People willing to try the odd roast

parts.note: to try something is to test it

indicators.note: odd says the letters of roast come out strangely arranged

explanation.surface: Some diners are game to sample a strange roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges ROAST into ATORS. 'People willing' means people making wills, not keen volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: Testators are those who make wills, so they are literally people engaged in willing property.

clue.text: The bench decide

definitions.meaning: a long wooden seat with a high back
to ... a matter is to resolve it

explanation.definitionFit: A settle is a high-backed wooden bench, and to settle a question is to resolve it.

clue.text: Suspect damp with decay

parts.note: mist is damp air
rust is the decay of iron

explanation.surface: A suspicion that the house has rising damp and rot.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect someone is to doubt or distrust them; both verbs.

clue.text: Permit to put an end to a singular state of affairs

definitions.text: Permit to put an end to a singular state of affairs

parts.words: Permit to put an end to a singular state of affairs
parts.note: a singular state is being single; the document that ends it is the official permission to wed

explanation.surface: Official permission sought to stop some odd goings-on.
explanation.definitionFit: This official document authorises a wedding, which ends a person's single life.

clue.text: For a blackleg taking on financial liabilities would be a bloomer

indicators.note: taking on means adding the next piece after the first

parts.note: a blackleg is a strikebreaker, also called a scab
IOUs are written promises to pay debts

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker who runs up debts would be making a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabious is a wild flower with pincushion heads, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Overcharges men on the board

definitions.meaning: to rook a customer is to swindle them

explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to cheat by charging too much, and chess has castle-shaped pieces of that name.

clue.text: Tries an ensemble for the fat…

indicators.note: an ensemble puts things together in a new grouping, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone attempts a musical group for the fat one.
explanation.definitionFit: Stearin is the main solid fat in tallow and suet.

clue.text: Puff at this point, but hold on

parts.note: a puff is a promotional advertisement, an ad
here means at this place

explanation.surface: Take a drag on a cigarette right now, but wait a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick or cling, as in keeping a grip.

clue.text: A red nose requires treatment, it's argued

indicators.note: letters needing treatment are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone claims a red nose needs medical attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasoned case is one set out logically, as an argument is.

clue.text: Some leftists would limit a Tory follower

indicators.note: some says only part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Left-wingers would like to rein in a Conservative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals a run inside 'limit a Tory'.
explanation.definitionFit: An imitator copies another, following their lead.

clue.text: Put in this month without hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is the old commercial term for the current month
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: Get it entered this month with no dithering.
explanation.definitionFit: To insert is to place something inside; both verbs.

clue.text: Curse a couple of articles written by the academic

parts.note: an is the indefinite article before a vowel
a is the other indefinite article
taken as written
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate academic

explanation.surface: Two newspaper pieces penned by a professor bring down a curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of articles' gives AN and A; 'written by' just joins them to THE and MA.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical ban or imprecation.

clue.text: A person into fruit, being a lover of good food

indicators.note: into means the first piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a gourd is a hard-skinned fruit
a man is a person

explanation.surface: Someone keen on fruit is a real food lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A gourmand enjoys eating, often to excess.

clue.text: … She finds a trim figure lacking in early spring!

indicators.note: in means the shortened phrase goes inside the month

parts.note: March is the first month of spring

indicators.note: lacking means a letter is taken out of the phrase before it

parts.note: taken as written
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A woman finds a slim figure missing at the start of spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes M out of A TRIM, giving ATRI, which goes into MARCH. The ellipsis links back to 7-down.
explanation.definitionFit: A matriarch is a female head of a family, a woman of authority.

clue.text: Caption causing a wrinkling of the brow?

definitions.meaning: a title over a news story

definitions.text: causing a wrinkling of the brow?
definitions.meaning: a furrow across the forehead, read literally as a crease on the top of the body

explanation.definitionFit: A headline is the title of a newspaper story, and playfully a crease line on one's forehead.

clue.text: A hard case in the main

definitions.text: A hard case in the main

parts.words: A hard case in the main
parts.note: the main is the sea; a hard case found there is a mollusc's protective covering

explanation.surface: A tough character, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' looks like 'mostly', and 'hard case' like a tough person; the main is the old word for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A mollusc's shell found by the sea is a hard protective casing.

clue.text: Draw for use of spare court

parts.note: a spare is an extra

explanation.surface: Raffle to decide who may use the spare tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw something out is to pull or remove it.

clue.text: Game remains in ring mould

indicators.note: in means the remains go inside the ring sound

parts.note: a ding is the ringing sound of a bell
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Leftover game meat set in a ring-shaped mould.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like hunted meat but means spirited. 'mould' completes the kitchen surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Game in the sense of spirited and plucky matches dashing, bold and lively.

clue.text: Space travel in peculiar contraption

indicators.note: a peculiar contraption is something oddly put together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Space travel in an odd machine.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a gap between two points.

clue.text: Such a belief, is held by the married

indicators.note: held by means the short word is gripped inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A conviction held by married couples.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god or gods.

clue.text: Maroon thread

definitions.meaning: to leave someone ..., as on an island

explanation.definitionFit: To strand someone is to abandon them, and a strand is a single filament.

clue.text: Warning a trainee to prepare for action

parts.note: L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
to arm is to make ready for battle

explanation.surface: A recruit is told to get ready for the fight.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is a signal of danger.

clue.text: They're all for viewers' clean-up endeavours

definitions.text: They're all for viewers' clean-up endeavours

parts.words: They're all for viewers' clean-up endeavours
parts.note: viewers are eyes, and the small cups here are used to rinse them

explanation.surface: Television audiences support efforts to tidy up the neighbourhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyebaths are small cups for bathing the eyes.

clue.text: A countryman is able to aid an organisation

parts.note: can means is able to

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A compatriot is able to help a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges AID into ADI, followed by AN as written. Countryman means a fellow national here, not a rustic.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian is a national of Canada.

clue.text: A supporter — but not for long!

definitions.meaning: one who backs a motion or a duellist

explanation.definitionFit: A second backs a duellist or boxer, and as a noun it is a very short spell of time.

clue.text: Stock running out?

parts.note: stock here is livestock, bolting all together in a panic

explanation.surface: A shop worried its supplies are exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden panicked rush of cattle.
